svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: osmosis in red blood cells
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Three red blood cells are put into solutions of different concentration."], [1, "In a more concentrated solution, water leaves the cell by osmosis: it shrinks and wrinkles (crenation)."], [4.5, "In an isotonic solution, water enters and leaves at the same rate: no change."], [7, "In pure water, water enters the cell by osmosis; animal cells have no cell wall, so it swells and bursts (haemolysis)."]]
svg.title: Red blood cells and osmosis
svg.desc: Red blood cells in a concentrated, an isotonic and a dilute solution: water leaves and the cell shrinks; no net change; water enters and the cell bursts.
svg.text: Blue dots: water molecules. Arrows: net movement of water.

g.data-info: Lower water potential outside: water leaves the cell by osmosis, so it shrinks and becomes crenated (wrinkled).
Water moves in and out at the same rate: no net movement, so the cell keeps its biconcave shape. Blood plasma is isotonic.

g.data-name: More dilute solution (hypotonic), e.g. pure water
g.data-info: Higher water potential outside: water enters by osmosis; with no cell wall the cell swells and bursts (haemolysis).
g.aria-label: More dilute solution (hypotonic), e.g. pure water

g.data-info: Lets water molecules through but not larger solute molecules.
g.text: Orange dots: solute (salt). Animal cells have only a partially permeable membrane, no cell wall.
